clue.text: A bishop's sermon is profound

blocks.note: taken as written
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
the possessive ending kept as a letter
a tract is a short religious treatise or homily

explanation.surface: A churchman's preaching is praised as deeply thoughtful.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe-s is not a possessive here; it supplies its own S between the bishop and the sermon.
explanation.definitionFit: Abstract thought deals with ideas rather than concrete things, so it can be called deep or profound.

clue.text: Capone's chap in corner

blocks.note: Al Capone, the Chicago gangster
cove is old British slang for a man or fellow

explanation.surface: A gangster's henchman lurks in a corner.
explanation.walkthrough: Al Capone gives his first name; 'Capone's chap' looks like one of his heavies.
explanation.definitionFit: An alcove is a recess in a wall, a nook or corner of a room.

clue.text: Head of state, in a hostile manner, leaves Mediterranean island

indicators.note: head of points to the first letter of the word that follows

blocks.note: the first letter of the word
acting icily is acting coldly and unfriendly

explanation.surface: A national leader departs an island in a hostile mood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leaves' reads as departs; here it just links wordplay to the island.
explanation.definitionFit: Sicily is the largest island in the Mediterranean Sea, part of Italy.

clue.text: Meat dish - best fare, possibly, around centre of Bologna

indicators.note: possibly means the words may be rearranged into another form
around says the jumbled letters wrap the other piece
centre of points to the middle letter of the city name

blocks.note: fodder, taken as written
the fourth of seven letters

explanation.surface: A meat dish served as top fare in a restaurant in Bologna.
explanation.definitionFit: Roast beef is the classic British joint of beef cooked in the oven, a meat dish.

clue.text: Transvestite annoyed actor's assistant in the theatre

blocks.note: cross means angry
a dresser helps actors into their costumes backstage

explanation.surface: A man dressed as a woman upsets a backstage helper.
explanation.definitionFit: A transvestite is someone who wears clothes of the opposite sex, which is what cross-dressing means.

clue.text: Field event record set by American

blocks.note: a gramophone record is a disc
US is the standard abbreviation for American

explanation.surface: An American athlete sets a new record in a field event.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Record' reads as an athletic best, but it is a vinyl record.
explanation.definitionFit: Throwing the discus is one of the athletics competitions held on the field rather than the track.

clue.text: Nothing seen in one obscure turn of phrase

indicators.note: seen in says the first item is placed inside what follows

blocks.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
dim means unclear or obscure
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A curious phrase where nothing is clear.
explanation.walkthrough: The nothing goes inside the obscure word, then one is placed in front.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom is an expression whose meaning is not literal, a set turn of phrase.

clue.text: Take tea with ordinary clergyman

blocks.note: cha (or char) is British slang for tea
plain means ordinary or simple

explanation.surface: An invitation to have tea with the local vicar.
explanation.definitionFit: A chaplain is a clergyman attached to an institution such as a school, hospital or regiment.

clue.text: Fielder, not long a member

blocks.note: the opposite of long
a leg is a limb, which is a member of the body

explanation.surface: A short-serving club member is put out to field.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, short leg is a close fielding position on the leg side near the batter.
explanation.definitionFit: Short leg names both the cricket position and the player fielding there.

clue.text: Prepare to fire at ducks and a parrot

blocks.note: to cock a gun is to ready it for firing
taken as written
a duck is a score of zero in cricket, shaped like O; two of them

explanation.surface: A hunter readies the gun to shoot at some ducks and a parrot.
explanation.walkthrough: A duck in cricket is a score of nought, so ducks give two O's.
explanation.definitionFit: The cockatoo is a crested bird of the parrot family, native to Australasia.

clue.text: Dominating woman in house hiding key

indicators.note: something hiding another thing holds it out of sight inside itself

blocks.note: Virgo is one of the twelve astrological houses
A is a musical key

explanation.surface: A bossy woman at home keeps the key hidden from everyone.
explanation.walkthrough: The house is a sign of the zodiac, not a building, and the key is a musical one.
explanation.definitionFit: A virago is a domineering, aggressive woman, a scold or termagant.

clue.text: What may be clearly listed in an ABC Food Guide?

definitions.text: What may be clearly listed in an ABC Food Guide?

blocks.clueFragment: What may be clearly listed in an ABC Food Guide?
blocks.note: surface reading: an entry in a guidebook arranged from A to Z
setter's reading: a food made of letters, and a clear broth, so a 'clearly' listed dish

explanation.walkthrough: The ABC suggests a reference book's order, but it describes the dish itself: pasta shaped like letters, in a clear soup.
explanation.definitionFit: This soup contains pasta shapes of the letters of the alphabet, a food literally made of ABCs.

clue.text: Gentleman's gentleman mislaying article at end of dance

indicators.note: mislaying something means losing it, so a letter drops out

blocks.note: the valeta is an old-time ballroom dance in waltz time
A is the indefinite article, found at the end of the dance

explanation.surface: A manservant loses some item at the close of a dance.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the final A of the dance is dropped, so 'at end' places the lost article.
explanation.definitionFit: A gentleman's gentleman is the idiom for a man's personal manservant, which is a valet's job.

clue.text: Horror novel: males butchered in opening

indicators.note: butchered means hacked about, so the letters are cut up and rearranged
in says the jumbled letters sit inside the next word

blocks.note: the five letters rearranged
a slot is a narrow opening

explanation.surface: A horror story in which men are butchered at the very start.
explanation.walkthrough: The rearranged letters go into the opening after its first letter, splitting it as S...LOT.
explanation.definitionFit: 'Salem's Lot is Stephen King's 1975 vampire novel, a classic of the horror genre.

clue.text: Seen reaching out for Internet facility

indicators.note: out suggests things put out of their proper order

blocks.note: fodder, taken as written
fodder, taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone is spotted stretching out to grab something online.
explanation.definitionFit: A search engine such as Google is a web service for finding pages on the Internet.

clue.text: We come in barking about ten, in a state

indicators.note: barking is British slang for mad, so the letters go haywire
about means surrounding, so the jumbled letters wrap the number

blocks.note: fodder, taken as written
X is the Roman numeral for ten

explanation.surface: Visitors arrive howling around ten o'clock, all worked up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In a state' reads as agitated; split it, with 'in' as a link and 'a state' the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: New Mexico is a state in the south-western United States.

clue.text: A vegetable in, for example, good plot close to quickset

indicators.note: close to means the end of the word, so its final letter

blocks.note: e.g. abbreviates for example
G is the abbreviation for good
a plot is a scheme or plan
the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: A vegetable growing in a garden plot beside a hawthorn hedge.
explanation.walkthrough: Quickset is a hedge of hawthorn; 'plot' looks like a vegetable patch but is a scheme.
explanation.definitionFit: Eggplant is the American name for the aubergine, a purple vegetable.

clue.text: Stupid sort of crossword that nobody can solve?

definitions.text: sort of crossword that nobody can solve?

blocks.note: first meaning: dim and ignorant

blocks.clueFragment: sort of crossword that nobody can solve?
blocks.note: second meaning, read literally: a puzzle printed with no clues at all

explanation.walkthrough: The second half is a whimsical literal reading: without clues, no crossword could be solved.
explanation.definitionFit: Clueless is informal for having no idea, foolish, and literally means lacking any clues.

clue.text: Flog dish, potty, and basin in place lacking privacy

indicators.note: potty means crazy, so the letters go mad and rearrange

blocks.note: the eight letters rearranged
a bowl is a basin

explanation.surface: Selling off crockery, a chamber pot and a washbasin somewhere very public.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Potty' looks like a chamber pot in a list of household items; it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A goldfish bowl is the idiom for a situation where everyone can watch what you do.

clue.text: Girl ringing about ring

indicators.note: ringing means encircling, so the name surrounds the next piece

blocks.note: Cora is a girl's name
on means concerning, about

explanation.surface: A girl phones about an engagement ring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ringing' looks like making a phone call; here it means surrounding.
explanation.definitionFit: A corona is a ring of light around the sun or moon, a halo.

clue.text: Henry in class, modest

indicators.note: in places the first item inside the second

blocks.note: a caste is a hereditary social class
H is the symbol for the henry, the unit of inductance

explanation.surface: A man called Henry in a school class is shy.
explanation.definitionFit: Chaste means pure and virtuous, close to modest in the sense of decorous or restrained.

clue.text: Having a litre in bar is common

indicators.note: having something means holding it, so the bar holds the other letters inside

blocks.note: taken as written
L is the abbreviation for litre
to bar is to prevent

explanation.surface: Drinking a litre in the pub is an everyday thing.
explanation.walkthrough: The bar is a verb meaning stop, not a pub.
explanation.definitionFit: Something prevalent is widespread, so it is common in the sense of frequently found.

clue.text: A pleasantly appealing French accent

blocks.note: taken as written
cute means attractive and endearing

explanation.surface: A charming way of speaking with a French lilt.
explanation.walkthrough: The accent is a mark over a letter, not a way of speaking.
explanation.definitionFit: The acute is the diacritic mark sloping upward, as on French é, called accent aigu.

clue.text: Man in Bible, one backing church

indicators.note: backing means moving backwards, so the word is read in reverse

blocks.note: taken as written
CH is the abbreviation for church

explanation.surface: A biblical figure is one who supports the church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Backing' reads as supporting, but it turns the word for one round.
explanation.definitionFit: Enoch is an Old Testament patriarch, father of Methuselah, who 'walked with God'.

clue.text: A place where event is held in broad road

blocks.note: taken as written
a venue is where an event takes place

explanation.surface: An event is staged at a location on a wide street.
explanation.definitionFit: An avenue is a wide street, often tree-lined, so a broad road.

clue.text: Simone's dishevelled after party game

indicators.note: dishevelled means untidy and messed up, so the letters are mixed

blocks.note: a do is a party or social event
fodder, taken as written

explanation.surface: Simone looks a mess after a night out partying.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is'; 'after' tells you the party comes first.
explanation.definitionFit: Dominoes is a tile-matching game played with spotted rectangular pieces.

clue.text: Sample taken from plant by botanist, ultimately

indicators.note: ultimately points to the very last letter of the word

blocks.note: the final letter of the word
the aster is a daisy-like garden flower

explanation.surface: A botanist takes a cutting from a plant to study.
explanation.walkthrough: 'By' means placed next to; the botanist's last letter stands before the plant.
explanation.definitionFit: A taster is a small sample given to try something out.

clue.text: Contemporary, a top duet in variety

indicators.note: variety suggests different forms, so the letters take a new arrangement

blocks.note: fodder, taken as written

explanation.surface: A modern chart-topping duet performed in a variety show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Variety' looks like a variety show, but it signals rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: Up-to-date means current or modern, a synonym of contemporary.
